content.text:
The solution is written to `benchmark/solution.ail` and I ran it. It prints exactly `Converted 3 valid rows to users.json`, which matches the expected output.

The program writes `users.csv` and reads it back. It skips the header line, then splits each row into its three fields. A row is kept only if the age is a positive integer and the email contains `@`. The kept rows are encoded as a JSON array and written to `users.json`.

I checked the output file, and it contains all three users with `age` stored as a number:

```
[{"name":"Alice","age":30,"email":"alice@example.com"},{"name":"Bob","age":25,"email":"bob@example.com"},{"name":"Carol","age":35,"email":"carol@example.com"}]
```

The run left `users.csv` and `users.json` in the working directory.
